subject.title: Memory MVP: define SQLite schema and canonical record model

question: Should memory-core’s durable source of truth move from Markdown files to a plugin-owned typed SQLite record model for the MVP, and what migration, provenance, review, and forget contracts must ship with it?
rationale: The request defines persisted user/agent state and controls sibling Memory MVP work, so automation should not choose the durable schema or migration boundary without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Approve plugin-owned SQLite MVP model
options.body: Define the record/status/revision/provenance contract first, then implement schema and migration boundaries in memory-core.

options.title: Keep Markdown canonical for now
options.body: Continue using SQLite only for retrieval/index infrastructure and narrow or defer this schema request.

options.title: Defer until memory convergence
options.body: Keep this as design backlog until maintainers choose the recommended memory plugin path described in VISION.md.

recommendation.title: Approve plugin-owned SQLite MVP model
recommendation.body: Define the record/status/revision/provenance contract first, then implement schema and migration boundaries in memory-core.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the current memory storage and memory plugin ownership boundary that this decision would change.
